fatal_errors: The proposed HIP treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention of liquid-metal dealloying a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
It omits the target bicontinuous RHEA-ligament/Cu-channel architecture and the spontaneously formed W-rich passivating interlayer.
It provides no irradiation-resistance mechanism, irradiation boundary, or comparison with pure W under helium implantation, despite irradiation being central to the requested service context.

The cited evidence concerns powder processing of unrelated Co-Cr-Cu-Fe-Ni and Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloys and does not substantiate HIP of W-Cu, pore closure, interface strengthening, or thermal-conductivity improvement.
The proposed 1100-1200 °C HIP range is above the melting point of Cu, yet the hypothesis does not address liquid-Cu containment, redistribution, leakage, or architecture loss.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes residual porosity and imperfect interfaces as relevant W-Cu fabrication problems and supplies a straightforward HIP-versus-no-HIP experiment with measurable falsification criteria. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target study: the target uses selective liquid-metal dealloying of an equiatomic WTaVTi alloy at 1200 °C for 96 h to replace Ti/V-rich channels with Cu while retaining aligned refractory-alloy ligaments. The generated mechanism is generic pressure-assisted densification rather than selective Ti-Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V, and W-rich interfacial passivation. Its predicted outcomes also omit the distinctive temperature-dependent thermal-conductivity crossover above approximately 650 °C and the qualified helium-swelling comparison against pure W. Baselines are named but underspecified, boundaries do not cover high-temperature thermal service or irradiation, and mechanical durability is asserted rather than linked to relevant evidence. Most importantly, neither citation supports the proposed W-Cu HIP intervention, making the otherwise testable alternative insufficiently evidenced.
